questions.q: What is the capital of Haiti?
questions.why: It was struck by a huge earthquake in 2010.

questions.q: In which year did Haiti become independent from France?
questions.why: It was the first free Black republic.

questions.q: Which revolution was the only successful slave revolt to create a nation?
questions.why: It lasted from 1791 to 1804.

questions.q: Which leader of the revolution is called 'the Black Napoleon'?
questions.why: He died in a French prison in 1803.

questions.q: Who declared Haiti's independence in 1804?
questions.why: He became Emperor Jacques I.

questions.q: What are Haiti's two official languages?
questions.why: Most Haitians speak Creole at home.

questions.q: Which family ruled Haiti as dictators from 1957 to 1986?
questions.why: They were 'Papa Doc' and 'Baby Doc'.

questions.q: Which king built the Citadelle Laferrière mountain fortress?
questions.why: It is a UNESCO site.

questions.q: Which priest became Haiti's first democratically elected President, in 1990?
questions.why: He was overthrown twice.

questions.q: Which country occupied Haiti from 1915 to 1934?
questions.why: US Marines ran the country.

questions.q: Which 1791 ceremony is said to have launched the revolution?
questions.why: It took place in the north.

questions.q: Which President was assassinated in 2021?
questions.why: He was killed at his home.

questions.q: Which battle in 1803 was the last major victory over the French?
questions.why: 18 November is a national holiday.

questions.q: What did France demand from Haiti in 1825 for recognising independence?
questions.why: It took Haiti until 1947 to pay it off.

questions.q: What was Haiti called as a French colony?
questions.why: It was France's richest colony.

questions.q: What is Haiti's currency?
questions.why: Its code is HTG.

questions.q: Which island does Haiti share with the Dominican Republic?
questions.why: Haiti is on the western third.

questions.q: Which religion, blending West African and Catholic traditions, is officially recognised in Haiti?
questions.why: It is officially recognised.

questions.q: Which soup is eaten on Independence Day, 1 January?
questions.why: It was once reserved for enslavers.

questions.q: What are the colourful hand-painted buses of Haiti called?
questions.why: Passengers tap to get off.

questions.q: Which artform shows Haiti's rich painting tradition?
questions.why: It often shows markets and village life.

questions.q: Which sea lies south of Haiti?
questions.why: The Atlantic lies to the north.

questions.q: Which northern city was the capital of King Henri Christophe?
questions.why: The Citadelle is nearby.

questions.q: Which palace ruins near the Citadelle belonged to King Henri?
questions.why: It was damaged by an 1842 earthquake.

questions.q: Which seaside town is famous for papier-mâché carnival masks?
questions.why: It is an arts centre.

questions.q: Which crop is Haiti among the world's top exporters of?
questions.why: It is used in perfumes.

questions.q: Which Haitian-American author wrote 'Breath, Eyes, Memory'?
questions.why: It was an Oprah's Book Club pick.

questions.q: Which Haitian music style is popular across the French Caribbean?
questions.why: Nemours Jean-Baptiste pioneered it in the 1950s.

questions.q: Which Haitian writer wrote 'Masters of the Dew'?
questions.why: It was published in 1944.

questions.q: Which deep-fried pork dish is a Haitian favourite?
questions.why: It is served with pikliz, a spicy slaw.
